blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: The Colors of Autumn
blocks.body:
Every autumn, the leaves of many trees turn brilliant shades of yellow, orange, and red. For a long time, people assumed that these colors ( 19 ). In fact, however, the yellow and orange colors are present in the leaves all summer long. They are simply hidden by chlorophyll, the green substance that plants use to make food from sunlight.
As the days become shorter and colder, trees stop producing chlorophyll. As the green color fades, the yellow and orange that were there all along ( 20 ). Red colors are different. They are produced only in autumn, when some trees create new chemicals in their leaves. Scientists are still debating why trees spend energy making red colors just before the leaves fall. One theory is that the red chemicals act like sunscreen, protecting the leaves while the tree ( 21 ).

qs.ex: In fact, however で「実は夏の間ずっと存在していた」と否定しているので、以前の考えは「秋に新しく作られる」。
緑が薄れると、ずっとあった黄色やオレンジが「見えるようになる」。
葉が落ちる前に、木が葉から「栄養を回収する」間の日焼け止めという説です。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Being Watched
blocks.body:
In the 1920s, researchers at the Hawthorne Works, a factory near Chicago, carried out a series of experiments to find out how working conditions affected productivity. In one study, they changed the brightness of the lights in a work area. To their surprise, workers' productivity ( 22 ), whether the lights were made brighter or dimmer. Even when the lighting was returned to its original level, output remained high.
The researchers eventually concluded that the workers were responding not to the changes themselves but to ( 23 ). Knowing that they were being studied, the workers may have tried harder than usual. This idea later became known as the Hawthorne effect.
Today, the Hawthorne effect is an important concern in scientific research. If people change their behavior simply because they know they are being observed, the results of a study may be misleading. ( 24 ), researchers often design experiments so that participants do not know exactly what is being measured.

qs.ex: To their surprise と、明るくしても暗くしても、元に戻しても生産量が高いままだったことから「向上した」。

o: the longer breaks they were given
the new machines in the factory
qs.ex: 研究されていると知って努力した=「注目されていること」に反応していた。
観察されていると行動が変わる問題を「避けるために」、何を測っているか知らせない設計にします。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: The Birth of Instant Noodles
blocks.body:
In 1958, a Japanese businessman named Momofuku Ando introduced the world's first instant noodles, called Chicken Ramen. Ando had lost his business after the Second World War, and he was moved by the sight of hungry people standing in long lines in the cold to buy bowls of ramen at black-market food stalls. He became determined to create a food that was cheap, tasty, and could be prepared easily at home.
Working alone in a small shed behind his house, Ando experimented for about a year. His breakthrough came when he watched his wife making tempura. He realized that frying noodles in hot oil would remove their moisture and leave tiny holes in them. The dried noodles could then be stored for a long time, and when hot water was poured over them, the holes allowed the water to soak in quickly, making them soft again in just a few minutes.
Chicken Ramen was at first considered a luxury, as it cost about six times more than fresh noodles at the time. Nevertheless, it soon became extremely popular. In 1971, Ando introduced Cup Noodles, which came in a container that could be used as both a cooking pot and a bowl. The idea came to him during a trip to the United States, where he noticed people breaking the noodles into cups and eating them with forks. Today, more than 100 billion servings of instant noodles are eaten around the world every year.

qs.q: What inspired Ando to create instant noodles?
o: A trip to the United States.
Seeing hungry people waiting in line for ramen.
qs.ex: 寒い中ラーメンを買うために長い列に並ぶ人々の姿に心を動かされました。アメリカ旅行はカップヌードルのきっかけです。

qs.q: How did frying the noodles help?
o: It dried them and let hot water soak in quickly.
It made them cheaper to produce.
It gave them a stronger chicken flavor.
It made them easier to cut into pieces.
qs.ex: 油で揚げると水分が抜けて小さな穴ができ、お湯がすぐしみこむようになりました。

qs.q: What gave Ando the idea for Cup Noodles?
o: Japanese customers asked for a smaller size.
People in the United States ate the noodles from cups.
His factory had too many cups.
A restaurant in Osaka used cups for soup.
qs.ex: アメリカで、めんを割ってカップに入れ、フォークで食べる人を見たことがきっかけです。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Breathing at 10,000 Meters
blocks.body:
When a passenger plane cruises at around 10,000 meters, the air outside is extremely thin. At that height, the air pressure is only about a quarter of that at sea level, and a person who was suddenly exposed to it would lose consciousness within a minute or so. To keep passengers safe and comfortable, airplanes pump air into the cabin to raise the pressure. However, the cabin is not pressurized to sea level. Instead, most planes keep the cabin at a pressure similar to that found at an altitude of about 2,400 meters, roughly the height of a high mountain town.
The reason is the strength of the aircraft. The greater the difference between the pressure inside and outside the plane, the stronger and heavier the body of the plane must be. For most healthy passengers, the slightly lower pressure causes no problems, although some people notice that their ears pop or that they feel tired more quickly than usual.
Where does the air come from? On most airliners, fresh air is taken in through the engines, cooled, and then mixed with air that has already been used in the cabin. Before it is recirculated, this used air passes through special filters that remove more than 99 percent of bacteria and viruses. As a result, the cabin air is completely replaced every few minutes. One drawback, however, is that the air at high altitude contains very little moisture, so cabin air is often drier than that of a desert, which can cause dry eyes and skin.
Newer aircraft have begun to address these problems. The Boeing 787, for example, is built mainly of carbon-fiber materials rather than aluminum. Because these materials are stronger and do not rust, the cabin can be kept at a pressure equal to an altitude of about 1,800 meters, and the air can be kept more humid. According to the manufacturer, passengers on such planes report fewer headaches and less tiredness after long flights.

qs.q: Why are most cabins not pressurized to sea level?
o: It would make the cabin too warm.
It would use too much fuel for air conditioning.
The body of the plane would need to be much stronger and heavier.
qs.ex: 内外の気圧差が大きいほど機体を強く重くしなければならないからです。

qs.q: What happens to used cabin air?
o: It is cleaned with filters and mixed with fresh air.
It is heated by the engines and reused only once.
It is kept in tanks until the plane lands.
qs.ex: 細菌やウイルスを99%以上取り除くフィルターを通し、新鮮な空気と混ぜて再循環させます。

qs.q: What is one disadvantage of cabin air?
o: It is replaced only once per flight.
It is colder than the air outside.
qs.ex: cabin air is often drier than that of a desert とあります。

qs.q: What is true about the Boeing 787?
o: It is made mainly of aluminum.
It flies lower than other airliners.
Its cabin can be kept at a pressure similar to a lower altitude.
Its passengers do not need to wear seat belts.
qs.ex: 炭素繊維の機体のため、客室を約1,800メートル相当の気圧に保てます。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は60語〜70語です。
parts.body:
In recent years, more businesses have started using a system called dynamic pricing, in which prices change frequently depending on demand. Airlines and hotels have used this method for many years, but now it is also being used for concert tickets, theme parks, and even some restaurants. Computer programs analyze data, such as how many people are searching for a product, and adjust prices automatically.
Supporters say that dynamic pricing benefits both businesses and customers. Companies can earn more when demand is high, and they can attract customers by lowering prices when demand is low. People who are flexible about when they travel or go out can therefore save money.
However, many consumers dislike the system. They feel it is unfair when the price of the same ticket rises suddenly just because many people want it. In addition, because prices keep changing, it can be difficult for customers to plan their budgets.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Dynamic pricing, in which computer programs change prices frequently according to demand, has spread from airlines and hotels to concerts, theme parks, and restaurants. It allows companies to earn more during busy periods and attract customers with lower prices when demand is low, helping flexible customers save money. However, many people think sudden price rises are unfair, and constantly changing prices make budgeting difficult.
checks: ダイナミックプライシングとは何か(需要で価格が変わる・広がっている)が入っている
利点(企業の収益・柔軟な客は節約できる)が入っている
問題点(不公平感・予算が立てにくい)が入っている
本文をそのまま写さず、言いかえて短くまとめている
語数が60〜70語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Should Japanese schools start the school year in September?

POINTS
・International exchange
・Cost
・Tradition
rules: 語数の目安は120語〜150語です。
構成は、序論・本論・結論が望ましい。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model:
I believe that Japanese schools should start the school year in September, for two main reasons.
First, it would make it easier for students to study abroad. Most universities in Europe and North America begin their academic year in September, so Japanese students who want to study overseas often lose several months. If Japan followed the same calendar, students could move between countries more smoothly, and more international students would come to Japan.
Second, the change would reduce the stress of entrance exams in winter. At present, important exams are held in January and February, when many students catch colds or the flu. Holding them in early summer would allow students to take tests in better health.
In conclusion, because a September start would encourage international exchange and create a healthier exam season, Japan should adopt it.
checks: 序論で自分の立場(賛成/反対)をはっきり述べている
POINTSなどを使った理由を2つ、具体例とともに書いている
本論の各段落が First / Second で始まり、構成がわかる
結論で立場と理由をまとめ直している
語数が120〜150語になっている

lines: Hi, Karen. I heard you're organizing the charity run next month. How's it going?
Pretty well, but we're still short of volunteers for the water stations.
I'd be glad to help. What time would I need to be there?
Around seven in the morning. The race starts at eight.
That's early, but I can manage. Put me down for it.
items.q: What will the man do?
items.ex: 給水所のボランティアを引き受けました。

lines: Excuse me, I ordered the vegetarian pasta, but this has bacon in it.
Oh, I'm terribly sorry. The kitchen must have made a mistake. I'll have a new one made right away.
How long will that take? I have to be back at the office in twenty minutes.
About ten minutes. Or, if you prefer, I could pack it to go when it's ready, and there'll be no charge.
items.q: What will the woman probably do?
o: Take a new pasta back to her office.
Go back to the office without any food.
items.ex: 作り直したパスタを持ち帰り用にしてもらい、無料で会社に持って帰ります。

lines: Sarah, have you finished reviewing the contract from Lambert Industries?
Almost. There's one clause about delivery dates that worries me. If we're late, we'd have to pay a huge penalty.
Hmm. Our supplier has been unreliable lately.
Exactly. I think we should ask them to extend the deadlines by two weeks before we sign.
Good idea. Can you draft an email to them?
items.q: What is the woman worried about?
o: The price in the contract is too low.
The company might have to pay a penalty for late delivery.
The supplier wants to end its contract.
The contract has already been signed.
items.ex: 納期に遅れると多額の違約金を払う条項を心配しています。

lines: Daniel, I noticed you've been staying late at the office every night this week.
Yes, I'm trying to finish the annual report by Friday.
You know, you could ask Tom to help. He finished his project early.
I didn't want to bother him.
I'm sure he wouldn't mind. And it's better than burning yourself out.
You're right. I'll talk to him this afternoon.
items.q: What will the man do this afternoon?
items.ex: 午後にトムに手伝いを頼むつもりです。

lines: Did you hear that the city is planning to build a new soccer stadium near the river?
Yes, but I'm not sure it's a good idea. That area floods almost every year.
They say they'll build walls to protect it.
Maybe, but that will make it even more expensive. I'd rather they spent the money on improving the hospital.
items.q: What does the woman think?
o: The river should be cleaned first.
The money should be used for the hospital.
The stadium will attract many tourists.
items.ex: I'd rather they spent the money on improving the hospital. と言っています。

lines: Hello, I'm calling about my internet service. It's been very slow for the past three days.
I'm sorry about that. Have you tried restarting your router?
There may be a problem with the line. I can send a technician on Wednesday morning.
I work from home, so the sooner the better. Is there anything earlier?
Unfortunately not. But I can give you a discount on this month's bill.
items.q: What does the man offer the woman?
o: A visit from a technician today.
items.ex: 早い修理はできないかわりに、今月の料金を割り引くと言っています。技術者が来るのは水曜日です。

lines: Mom, can I borrow the car this weekend? Some friends and I want to go to the beach.
That's a long drive. You only got your license last month.
I know, but Kevin has been driving for three years. We could take turns.
All right, as long as Kevin does most of the driving on the highway.
items.q: What condition does the mother set?
o: The boy must come home by Saturday night.
Kevin must do most of the highway driving.
They must take the train instead.
The boy must pay for the gas.
items.ex: as long as Kevin does most of the driving on the highway(高速道路はケビンが運転するなら)という条件です。

lines: Professor Kim, I'd like to change the topic of my thesis.
Oh? You've already done a lot of research on urban planning.
I know, but I've become really interested in renewable energy since my internship.
Changing topics now would mean starting almost from scratch. Have you thought about combining the two? For example, energy use in city design.
That's a great idea. I'll think about it.
items.q: What does the professor suggest?
o: Keeping her original topic without changes.
items.ex: 都市計画と再生可能エネルギーを組み合わせることを提案しています。

lines: I'm thinking of joining that new gym near the station.
The one with the swimming pool? I heard it's really expensive.
It is, but they're offering a 50 percent discount for the first three months.
That's good, but what happens after that? You might end up paying a lot for a gym you don't use.
True. I'll try their free one-week trial first and then decide.
items.q: What will the man do first?
items.ex: まず1週間の無料体験をしてから決めます。

lines: Excuse me, I'm supposed to meet a client at the Grand Hotel, but my phone's battery is dead, and I can't find the address.
The Grand Hotel? It's on Park Avenue, about fifteen minutes on foot. But it's starting to rain.
The number 6 goes there, but it only comes every half hour. I'd take a taxi. There's a taxi stand right around the corner.
items.q: What does the man recommend?
items.ex: I'd take a taxi. と勧めています。雨が降り出し、バスは30分に1本です。

lines: Hi, Emily. How was your first month at the new company?
Mostly good. The work is interesting, but my manager keeps sending emails late at night and expects quick replies.
That sounds stressful. Have you talked to him about it?
Not yet. I'm worried he'll think I'm not committed.
I think it's better to discuss it early, before it becomes a bigger problem.
items.q: What does the man advise Emily to do?
items.ex: 問題が大きくなる前に早めに上司と話すよう助言しています。

lines: Have you booked the hotel for the conference in Osaka?
Not yet. The hotel next to the venue is fully booked.
What about the one near Shin-Osaka Station? It's only two stops away by subway.
I checked, but it's twice as expensive. I found a cheaper place about 20 minutes away by train. I think I'll stay there.
items.q: Where will the man probably stay?
o: At the hotel next to the venue.
At a cheaper hotel 20 minutes away by train.
At a hotel near Shin-Osaka Station.
At a friend's house in Osaka.
items.ex: 電車で20分の安いホテルに泊まるつもりです。

lines: Why Airplane Windows Are Round. In 1952, the de Havilland Comet became the world's first jet airliner to carry passengers. However, within two years, two Comets broke apart in the air, and all of the planes were grounded. Investigators discovered that the problem was metal fatigue. Each time the plane was pressurized and depressurized, stress built up in the metal, especially around the sharp corners of its window openings. Eventually, small cracks formed there and spread. Since then, airplane windows have been designed with rounded corners, which spread stress more evenly.

qs.q: What happened to the Comet airliners?
o: They were too slow to compete.
Two of them broke apart in the air.
They could not fly at high altitudes.
They were too expensive to build.
qs.ex: two Comets broke apart in the air とあります。

qs.q: Why do airplane windows have rounded corners today?
o: They give passengers a better view.
They reduce noise from the engines.
qs.ex: 角が丸いと力(応力)が均等に分散され、ひびが入りにくくなります。

items.title: Why Airplane Windows Are Round

lines: The Leaning Tower of Pisa. Construction of the famous bell tower in Pisa, Italy, began in 1173. By the time builders had completed the third floor, the tower had already begun to lean, because the soft ground beneath it could not support its weight evenly. Work was then stopped for almost a century because of wars, which gave the soil time to settle and probably prevented the tower from falling. By 1990, however, the lean had become so serious that the tower was closed. Engineers carefully removed soil from under the higher side, and the tower was reopened in 2001, leaning slightly less than before.

qs.q: Why did the tower begin to lean?
o: The ground under it was soft.
It was hit by an earthquake.
It was damaged in a war.
qs.ex: the soft ground beneath it could not support its weight evenly とあります。

qs.q: What did engineers do in the 1990s?
o: They added more floors to the tower.
They moved the tower to a new location.
They removed soil from under one side.
They built a wall to support the tower.
qs.ex: 高い側の下から土を少しずつ取り除きました。

items.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa

lines: Clever Birds. New Caledonian crows, which live on islands in the South Pacific, are among the most intelligent animals in the world. In the wild, they make hooks from twigs and leaves and use them to pull insects out of holes in trees. In laboratory experiments, some crows have even solved puzzles that required using one tool to get another tool. Interestingly, young crows learn tool-making partly by watching their parents, which suggests that these birds can pass on skills from one generation to the next.

qs.q: How do New Caledonian crows use tools in the wild?
o: To pull insects out of holes.
qs.ex: 小枝や葉でかぎを作り、木の穴から虫を引き出します。

qs.q: How do young crows learn to make tools?
qs.ex: young crows learn tool-making partly by watching their parents とあります。

items.title: Clever Birds

lines: Standing Through Earthquakes. Japan has suffered countless earthquakes, yet very few of its traditional five-story wooden pagodas are known to have collapsed because of one. Engineers believe the secret lies in their design. Each story rests loosely on the one below it, so during an earthquake, the floors can sway in opposite directions, like a snake moving. At the center of the pagoda stands a thick wooden pillar called the shinbashira, which keeps the floors from moving too far. Some modern towers, including the Tokyo Skytree, use a similar central pillar to reduce shaking.

qs.q: What is special about traditional five-story pagodas?
o: Very few have collapsed in earthquakes.
qs.ex: 地震で倒れたことがほとんど知られていません。

qs.q: What does the Tokyo Skytree have in common with the pagodas?
o: A central pillar that reduces shaking.
Floors that rest loosely on each other.
qs.ex: 心柱(shinbashira)に似た中心の柱でゆれを抑えています。

items.title: Standing Through Earthquakes

lines: A Message to the Stars. In 1977, NASA launched two space probes, Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, to study the outer planets of our solar system. Each probe carries a gold-plated record containing sounds and images from Earth, including greetings in 55 languages, music from many cultures, and the sounds of waves and birds. The records were intended as a message to any intelligent beings who might find the probes in the distant future. Both probes eventually traveled beyond the planets, and for decades afterward they continued to send data back to Earth.

qs.q: What was the main purpose of the Voyager probes?
o: To search for life on Mars.
qs.ex: to study the outer planets of our solar system とあります。

qs.q: What is on the record carried by each probe?
o: The names of all NASA workers.
qs.ex: 55の言語のあいさつ、音楽、波や鳥の音など、地球の音と画像が入っています。

items.title: A Message to the Stars

lines: An Ancient Computer. In 1901, divers exploring a shipwreck near the Greek island of Antikythera found a lump of corroded bronze. Decades later, X-ray studies revealed that it contained more than 30 gear wheels. Researchers now believe that the device, made more than 2,000 years ago, was used to predict the positions of the sun, moon, and planets, as well as eclipses. Nothing as complex is known to have been built again for over a thousand years, which is why it is often called the world's first computer.

qs.q: How did researchers learn about the device's gears?
qs.ex: X-ray studies revealed that it contained more than 30 gear wheels とあります。

qs.q: What was the device used for?
o: Measuring the depth of the sea.
Predicting the movements of the sun, moon, and planets.
qs.ex: 太陽・月・惑星の位置や日食を予測するために使われたと考えられています。

items.title: An Ancient Computer

The museum will close in one hour, at 5 p.m. Our special dinosaur exhibition is open until closing time, but the last entry was at 4 p.m. The children's science workshop on the second floor starts at 4:15 and lasts 30 minutes. Students can also use the printers in the Student Center, which is a five-minute walk from here. Please note that the Student Center printers accept payment only by student ID card.
items.q: What should you do?

lines: We can send your suitcase to the airport for you.
